title: Lindsay Dusard
text:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in Quantitative Methods at the University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education. I will also obtain an A.M. in Statistics and Data Science from the Wharton School.
I am an applied researcher who focuses on intersections of immigration, social policy, and child and family well-being. My research is motivated and informed by more than 10 years of experience supporting newcomer children and their families and engages with partners across the nonprofit and public sectors. I leverage a range of advanced quantitative and mixed-methods approaches and draw on frameworks from multiple disciplines, including sociology, demography, psychology, economics, and education.
My primary line of research focuses on how immigration and social policies shape the academic, economic, and social outcomes of refugee children and families in the United States. My dissertation explores these students’ receipt of federal and state financial aid, participation in social safety net programs (i.e., SNAP, Medicaid, and TANF), and pursuit of postsecondary education in Virginia.
I am also interested in advancing methodological approaches that help us better understand underlying mechanisms and outcomes in social policy research. Recently, I have focused on text analysis and how participatory research approaches have been used to design and implement randomized controlled trials.
As a predoctoral fellow with the Institute of Education Sciences, I completed yearlong research placements with the Urban Institute’s Immigration Cross-Center Initiative and the International Rescue Committee.
I am on the 2026-2027 job market.
